critical.issue: Brute-force lockout never triggers when accessed through the public ingress. Backend keys lockout on request.client.host + email, but the ingress makes that value change per connection, so unlimited 401s are returned instead of 429 after 5 fails. Verified: 8 consecutive wrong-password attempts via REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL all returned 401; identical test on http://localhost:8001 returns 429 after 5. Fix: derive identifier from X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP (fallback to client.host).

critical_code_review_comments: auth.py login lockout uses request.client.host, which is a single k8s pod IP behind ingress -> effectively per-connection random for real users, so the lockout is silently bypassed in production. Use X-Forwarded-For first hop or throttle per-email.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout bypass — RCA: /app/backend/auth.py:161 builds ident='{request.client.host}:{email}'. Behind Kubernetes ingress, request.client.host is the reverse-proxy pod's socket peer, which is not stable per real end-user (different connections use different sidecar sockets) and is identical for ALL real users. Result: counters never accumulate for a single victim, so line 163 (>= MAX_FAILED) is never true. Reproduction: `for i in {1..8}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"nope@x.io","password":"wrong"}'; done` -> all 401. Same on http://localhost:8001 -> 5x401 then 429. Mitigation: prefer request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or throttle purely per-email (with a small IP salt) to defeat rotation.
